explanation: The statement concerns the ℤ-submodule `Submodule.span ℤ {(a : ℤ_[p])}` of ℤ_[p] and a specific witness `PadicInt.inv (p+1)`. I searched Mathlib's `NumberTheory/Padics/*` (PadicIntegers, RingHoms, ProperSpace, MahlerBasis, ValuativeRel, …) for span/membership results involving ℤ_[p], and grepped all of Mathlib for patterns like `∉ Submodule.span ℤ`, `span ℤ {(… : ℤ_[p])}`, `inv_succ`, `notMem_span_singleton`, `span_singleton_ne_top`. Mathlib only contains the ingredients used in the proof (PadicInt.inv, mul_inv, norm_natCast_eq_one_iff, intCast_eq, denseRange_intCast) and nothing about ℤ-singleton spans in ℤ_[p] or about nonmembership of `inv (p+1)`; the span-based results (`dense_int_span_of_isUnit_of_denseRange_intCast`, `topologicalClosure_eq_iInf_sup`) are this library's own. The proof is a multi-step argument (reducing membership to an integer product equal to 1 and excluding it by size), so it is not a one-line instance of any Mathlib declaration either.
